column1: # Phase 5b reviewed database-effect contract for the legacy web oracle.
# The oracle flow is not read-only: login creates or retrieves an MSession
# are then read back as defaults when the role/client/org/warehouse controls are
# rebuilt (RolePanel.java:304-419). Capture A could therefore change what capture
# B observes, so the allowed delta set is reviewed and asserted rather than
# Any effect outside this table fails the gate; it is not silently absorbed.

column4: Each capture logs in once, so exactly one session row is created. A different count means the flow changed shape (an extra or missing login) and the oracle would be rebased against a different session identity.

On a freshly restored seed the oracle user has no preference rows, so the first capture CREATES them; every later capture rewrites the same values in place. Asserting 'unchanged' was therefore only true on an already-warmed database and passed for the wrong reason. The contract instead pins the absolute post-capture digest, which is strictly stronger: it fails both on a changed role/client/org/warehouse selection and on a capture that never reached role completion at all.

Opening a window records an AD_RecentItem row, and the desktop menu renders the recent-items list. Each capture therefore changes what the NEXT capture renders, which makes the oracle order-dependent: the frozen desktop response showed one recent item and a later capture showed two. The fixture deletes the oracle user's recent items before every capture so each one starts from the same empty list. This was found by the frozen-tree diff, not by inspection.

Creating the oracle user's preference rows is change-logged, so the first capture on a freshly restored seed inserts AD_ChangeLog rows that reference its AD_Session. Later captures rewrite the same preference values, ADempiere logs no change, and the delta must be exactly zero. Every row the first capture inserts must belong to AD_Preference; a row for any other table means the flow touched something it was never reviewed to touch. Opening the menu also creates the user's AD_Tree_Favorite node on first login, which is logged the same way. Both effects were discovered by the gate failing -- the foreign key on adsession_adchangelog, then the undeclared-table assertion -- not by inspection, which is why the replay now primes a cold database instead of assuming a warm one.
The deep flow opens the "Error Message" window read-only and performs no record save, so no dictionary or transactional row is written. Measured across paired captures.
